items.t: "Steelhead" is an MLS® sub-area name for a rural community in the City of Mission, in the northwest of the city around Cardinal Street and the Steelhead Road / Stave Lake Street corridor. The guide page states it plainly: Steelhead is an MLS® sub-area name, the City of Mission doesn't publish a boundary for it, and the City's Rural Mission Strategy page names Steelhead among the rural communities it covers. No official boundary for the sub-area was found: UNVERIFIED as an official boundary. SnapStats lists "Steelhead" as a sub-area under Mission in the FVR extraction. Access runs from Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) north through Silverdale Avenue / Stave Lake Street and Steelhead Road to the Campbell, Sabo and Cardinal Street pockets shown in the guide page's feed. Listing text stating about 15 minutes to downtown Mission is listing copy, not an official source: commute times in minutes are UNVERIFIED.

Nearby areas: Stave Falls to the northeast (a separate sub-area in the same SnapStats table, and itself inside the City of Mission), Silverdale to the south and southwest, Mission West and the urban Mission core to the southeast, and Hayward Lake / Ruskin across the Stave River side to the south.
Both splits published an empty shelf for September 2026; a zero row in a small rural sub-area says nothing about values or demand and must not be read as a market signal.

Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere — there is no verified condo stock in Steelhead at all. The housing is rural acreage parcels with detached houses and manufactured homes on owned land, plus bare land: the guide feed's eight listings include a 4.6-acre parcel with a brand-new prefab home and a large shop (Sabo Street), a 5.5-acre view lot (Campbell Street), a 9.5-acre parcel with a drilled well and a nearly 9-acre parcel (both Cardinal Street), a manufactured home on Cardinal Street, and the one small Silverdale Avenue lot at the feed's south edge.

The nearest confirmed elementaries are Stave Falls Elementary (K–6), 30204 Brackley Avenue, in Stave Falls to the northeast, and Silverdale Elementary (K–6), 29715 Donatelli Avenue, in Silverdale to the south; Hatzic Middle School, 34875 Moffat Avenue, is the middle school the guide page names for Steelhead. SD75 catchments are set under the district's Catchment Areas policy, and no document opened states the catchment schools for a Steelhead address — address-level catchments are UNVERIFIED: confirm the exact address with the district.

The rail link for the city is the West Coast Express at Mission City Station, with weekday trains between Mission City and Waterfront (downtown Vancouver). Recreation anchor: BC Hydro's Hayward Lake recreation area, near Mission on the Stave River system — the reservoir is an active hydroelectric facility and a popular recreation area, with the Stave Lake boat launch and Ruskin Dam recreation area also BC Hydro sites; the City of Mission restricts parking on city roads leading to Hayward Lake at busy times. Health care: Mission Memorial Hospital, 7324 Hurd Street, Mission (Fraser Health).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Steelhead

items.t: Mission plan and zoning: Zoning is Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020: the rural area is divided into Rural zones RU80, RU36 and RU16, each with a Secondary Dwelling ("s") variant (RU80s, RU36s, RU16s), and Rural Residential zones RR7 / RR7s inside the Rural Residential designation; a City rezoning notice describes the RU16 zone as carrying a 1.6 ha minimum lot size, and City application material for the neighbouring Stave Falls area confirms RU16-to-RU16s rezonings are the route used to permit a secondary detached unit on a rural lot outside the Urban Growth Boundary on land designated Rural Residential. Any Steelhead parcel's actual zone is per-parcel: UNVERIFIED.

Secondary dwellings: a Mission secondary suite is a self-contained living space inside a single family home forming part of the same real estate entity; a suite is not a coach home or garden cottage (those are detached secondary dwellings); suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes; all suites must be registered with the City, new suites go through the building permit process, and an annual secondary suite fee of $63 plus utility fees applies. On rural lots, a detached second dwelling generally requires the "s" variant of the parcel's zone, obtained by rezoning.

Mission property tax penalty is a flat 10%: — City of Mission 2026 property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a 10% penalty added to any current balances outstanding (including unclaimed home owner grants) on July 3, 2026 (Community Charter ss. 233–234 + Municipal Tax Regulation, B.C. Reg. 426/2003, s. 3). This is the CITY regime, and Steelhead is inside the City of Mission; the staged 5% + 5% figures quoted for rural Fraser Valley land belong to the Taxation (Rural Area) Act regime for unincorporated areas and do NOT apply here.

Wells, septic and ALR: the guide feed's own listings show the area's servicing pattern — drilled wells, septic systems and propane heat on acreage parcels. Wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database, and onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation, including the 30 m setback from a well unless professional advice is obtained. ALR status is per-parcel — check the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)), which is one structural reason no ALR parcel here can become condo stock.

Manufactured homes and pad rent: the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act limits pad-rent increases in manufactured home parks (2026: 2.3% plus a proportional amount; 2027: 2.2% plus a proportional amount). Steelhead's manufactured homes in the feed are on owned land, not park pads, so the MHPTA regime does not apply to them — a buyer who wants park-tenure product is looking at a different sub-area and a different tenure entirely.

items.t: "Steelhead" is a board name the City barely publishes. The City of Mission doesn't publish a boundary for it; the City mention the guide page relies on is the Rural Mission Strategy page naming Steelhead among the rural communities it covers. Searches run under only the board name miss City documents filed under the rural zone framework (RU80 / RU36 / RU16) and the Stave Falls / Silverdale community names.

The feed quietly crosses into Silverdale. One of the eight feed listings is a Silverdale Avenue lot its own text places in the Silverdale lands, yet the feed labels it Steelhead — the board line between the two sub-areas at the south edge is UNCONFIRMED, and a buyer comparing "Steelhead" listings may be looking at two different school catchments and servicing areas.

Three live-page defects are on the record for this guide page (Jerry's list). (2) In the "Steelhead questions" FAQ, the question "How do I see current Steelhead listings?" appears with NO answer — the MLS® reciprocity disclaimer follows it instead, and no answer appears elsewhere in the page text read. (3) The quoted City tax-exemption notice spells "Recreational facilities and programs" (twice) — a typo carried in the quote as rendered on the page.

Stave Falls is inside the City of Mission — the neighbouring sub-area to the northeast is city land on the same rural rules, not a separate jurisdiction, even though it reads like a standalone village; its RU16-to-RU16s rezonings are the worked example Steelhead owners follow for a detached second dwelling.

Hydro shaped this valley before the houses did. Construction of the Stave Falls Dam and Powerhouse began in 1909 and was completed by January 1, 1912 (BC Hydro); Hayward Lake is an active hydroelectric reservoir first and a recreation area second, and the City restricts parking on the roads leading to it at busy times — summer access pressure is part of the ownership picture.

The two nearest elementary schools sit in two different communities. Stave Falls Elementary is northeast in Stave Falls and Silverdale Elementary is south in Silverdale, and SD75 catchments are set by district policy — a Steelhead address cannot be school-matched by community name alone.
The guide page's City claims are unverified site copy.

The hospital is in town, not out here. Mission Memorial Hospital, 7324 Hurd Street, provides 24/7 emergency stabilization and care, general medicine and ambulatory care (Fraser Health) — every service run from a Steelhead acreage is a drive to the urban core southeast.

items.t: Feed scope reaches Silverdale: one of the eight feed listings is a small lot on Silverdale Avenue described in its own text as being in the Silverdale lands, yet the feed labels it "Steelhead" — the page's feed scope and the neighbouring Silverdale area overlap at the south edge, and where the board draws the Steelhead/Silverdale line is UNVERIFIED. Nearby areas: Stave Falls to the northeast (a separate sub-area in the same SnapStats table), Silverdale to the south and southwest, Mission West and the urban Mission core to the southeast, and Hayward Lake / Ruskin across the Stave River side to the south.

Market context, labelled community context ONLY (SnapStats FVR Sep 2026; Mission IS a covered community — Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined only; land has NO SnapStats category and these are NOT land figures): Steelhead — Detached 0 / 0 / NA; Condos & Townhomes 0 / 0 / NA — a published empty shelf in both splits. Combined Mission community — Detached median $814,000; attached median $430,000, expressly NOT Steelhead figures. No Steelhead median is published: UNVERIFIED.

Nearest schools confirmed by name and address: Stave Falls Elementary (K–6), 30204 Brackley Avenue, in Stave Falls to the northeast; Silverdale Elementary (K–6), 29715 Donatelli Avenue, in Silverdale to the south; Hatzic Middle School, 34875 Moffat Avenue — the middle school the guide page names for Steelhead; the district's secondary school is Mission Senior Secondary, 32939 7th Avenue (never "École Mission Senior Secondary").
How people search for it: "Steelhead" (board name), "Steelhead, Mission," and "Steelhead Road" for the corridor.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Steelhead Mission Guide

items.t: OCP — City of Mission Official Community Plan Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted April 21, 2026: (settled program position).

Zoning — City of Mission Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020: the rural area divides into Rural zones RU80, RU36 and RU16, each with a Secondary Dwelling ("s") variant (RU80s, RU36s, RU16s), and Rural Residential zones RR7 / RR7s inside the Rural Residential designation; a City rezoning notice describes RU16 as carrying a 1.6 ha minimum lot size, and City application material for neighbouring Stave Falls confirms RU16-to-RU16s rezonings are the route used to permit a secondary detached unit on a rural lot outside the Urban Growth Boundary on land designated Rural Residential. Any Steelhead parcel's actual zone: per-parcel, UNVERIFIED.

Secondary suites and detached dwellings — Mission: a Mission secondary suite is a self-contained living space inside a single family home forming part of the same real estate entity; a suite is not a coach home or garden cottage (those are detached secondary dwellings); suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes; all suites must be registered with the City, new suites go through the building permit process, and an annual secondary suite fee of $63 plus utility fees applies. On rural lots, a detached second dwelling generally requires the "s" variant of the parcel's zone, obtained by rezoning where the parcel does not already carry it.

SSMUH — Mission: Mission's SSMUH incorporation is Bylaw 6299-2024 (July 17, 2024), verified via City sources; zones previously restricted to single-family or duplex dwellings as of December 7, 2023 are subject to the provincial framework, subject to eligibility and servicing. Whether SSMUH unit counts apply to a given Steelhead lot is per-parcel: UNCONFIRMED — Steelhead's rural lots sit outside the urban serviced area, Mission unit counts for this ground remain UNCONFIRMED, and Surrey figures are never imported here. Do not price a Steelhead acreage on urban SSMUH unit counts.

Subdivision and servicing — Mission: Mission's Development and Subdivision Control Bylaw is 5650-2017 (DSCB 5650-2017 — stated from a City source found in workstream L10; title confirmed on mission.ca in L11; carried with that sourcing). Subdivision potential follows the parcel's rural zone minimums (RU16 at 1.6 ha per the City notice) and, where ALR applies, ALC approval (ALR block below). Servicing on this ground is well and septic: wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database, and onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation, including the 30 m setback from a well unless professional advice is obtained.

Property taxes — City of Mission (Steelhead is city land, stated expressly): City of Mission 2026 property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a FLAT 10% penalty added to any current balances outstanding (including unclaimed home owner grants) on July 3, 2026 (Community Charter ss.233–234 + Municipal Tax Regulation, B.C. Reg. 426/2003, s.3; Mission has NO alternative-scheme bylaw under Charter s.235). The FVRD rural regime — Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11, 5% after July 2 + 5% after October 31 — does NOT apply to a Steelhead parcel; the two regimes are different and are never blended.

ALR block (applies where a Steelhead parcel is ALR — status per-parcel, UNVERIFIED here): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). No ALR parcel count or split for Steelhead is documented, and none is invented; check a parcel on the ALC maps.

blocks.text: Good to know about Steelhead Mission Guide

items.t: Recreation access is the value story (BC Hydro, read Nov 1, 2026). BC Hydro's Hayward Lake recreation area, on the Stave River system, is the area's anchor recreation site — the reservoir is an active hydroelectric facility and a popular recreation area — and the City of Mission restricts parking on city roads leading to Hayward Lake at busy times, so summer access pressure is part of the ownership picture. Hydroelectric development shaped the Stave valley from 1909 (Stave Falls Dam and Powerhouse construction began 1909, completed by January 1, 1912).

Well and septic records are subject-removal items here (Nov 1, 2026). The feed's own listings run on drilled wells and septic systems; wells sit in the provincial GWELLS database, and sewerage systems must meet the Sewerage System Regulation's setbacks (including 30 m from a well unless professional advice is obtained) — pull both records on every deal, not in closing week.

Guide-only claims (the Cardinal Street rezoning proposal's status, the Steelhead Community Association / hall listing, the Municipal Forest figures, the Rural Mission Strategy approval date, the Cardinal Street flooding account, and the 2011 Mission ALR inventory figure of 1,539 hectares) are UNVERIFIED site copy, not defects and not facts.
The empty-shelf conflict, restated (Sep–Nov 2026).

faq.a: Steelhead is a rural acreage community in the City of Mission, on the Stave Lake / Steelhead Road side west of the urban core — SnapStats lists it as an FVREB sub-area under Mission, and the live page describes larger rural lots and forested settings with access toward Stave Falls and Hayward Lake, distinct from the Stave Falls waterfront market (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: What sold in Steelhead in September 2026?
faq.a: Nothing, as published: detached recorded 0 listings and 0 solds, and Condos & Townhomes recorded 0 listings and 0 solds, so no sales ratio applies — an empty shelf in a small rural sub-area, not a value signal. At the Mission community level the detached median sale price was $814,000 and the Condos & Townhomes median was $430,000 (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Can a Steelhead acreage have a suite or a second dwelling?
faq.a: An in-house secondary suite is permitted inside a single family home if it is registered with the City (new suites need a building permit; a $63 annual suite fee plus utility fees applies), but a detached coach home or garden cottage is a secondary detached dwelling — on rural lots that generally requires the secondary-dwelling ("s") variant of the parcel's zone, which City material shows owners obtaining by rezoning (e.g., RU16 to RU16s).

faq.q: What recreation is Steelhead known for?
faq.a: BC Hydro's Hayward Lake recreation area — a hydroelectric reservoir and popular recreation area near Mission, with the Stave Lake boat launch and Ruskin Dam recreation area nearby — plus the Stave Falls Powerhouse visitor facilities; the City of Mission restricts parking on the roads leading to Hayward Lake at busy times.

faq.q: Are there any condos in Steelhead?
faq.a: The attached market for Mission is in the urban core, not in this rural sub-area.

faq.q: Is a manufactured home on acreage here a condo or a park home?
faq.a: Neither. The feed's manufactured homes sit on their own land — one listing states expressly "on its own land (not in a park, no pad rent)" — so the purchase is freehold land plus the home, with no strata fees and no pad rent. Financing, insurance and depreciation treatment differ from both strata and park product; confirm with the lender before writing.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Steelhead acreage?
faq.a: The nearest elementaries are Stave Falls Elementary (30204 Brackley Avenue) and Silverdale Elementary (29715 Donatelli Avenue), the middle schools are Hatzic Middle and École Heritage Park Middle (7–9), and the secondary school is Mission Senior Secondary (32939 7th Avenue) — but the catchment for a specific Steelhead address is UNVERIFIED, so confirm the address with School District 75.

faq.q: How is a Steelhead property serviced?
faq.a: On the feed's evidence: drilled well, septic system and propane heat are the pattern on acreage parcels. Pull the well record from the provincial GWELLS database and the septic history on every deal — the Sewerage System Regulation's setbacks (including 30 m from a well unless professional advice is obtained) are subject-removal items here, not closing-week surprises.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or a coach house?
faq.a: An in-house secondary suite can be registered with the City (new suites need a building permit; a $63 annual suite fee plus utility fees applies), but suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes, and a detached coach home or garden cottage is a secondary detached dwelling — on rural lots that generally requires the secondary-dwelling ("s") variant of the parcel's zone, obtained by rezoning (City material shows RU16 owners rezoning to RU16s for exactly this).

faq.q: Are there any townhouses in Steelhead?
faq.a: None verified — zero strata, zero fee-simple, and no named townhome complex confirmed on an official source.

faq.q: Which Mission townhouse complexes can I actually search by name?
faq.a: The four assembled city-wide: Cherry Lane and Luther Place on 7th Avenue, Briskham Hill on Briskham Street, and Archer Green in Mission West.

faq.q: Is Luther Place a condo or a townhouse?
faq.a: A townhouse — the MLS dwelling-type field says Townhouse, Strata Plan NWS2729, 36 units, built 1988, and that field governs over the "Condos" filing some listing feeds use.
